# Ruby 1.9.2-p0, vendored for vkxp

This directory is a subset of the Ruby 1.9.2 patch level 0 release (revision 29036), kept at
its original relative paths. `vkxp-ruby192-sys` compiles it into the interpreter for the
scripts of RPG Maker VX Ace (RGSS3), whose original runtime embeds this very release.

## Origin

- Release: `ruby-1.9.2-p0.tar.gz`, from
  `https://cache.ruby-lang.org/pub/ruby/1.9/ruby-1.9.2-p0.tar.gz`
- SHA-256 of the tarball:
  `8c0c4e261a921b5c406bf9e76ac23bf3c915651534e9d1b9e8c5d0bee4a7285c`

`MANIFEST.sha256` lists the upstream SHA-256 of every vendored file, in the format of
`sha256sum`. `PATCHES.md` lists every local change, and `patches/` holds the diffs. A test in
`vkxp-ruby-sys` (`tests/manifest.rs`) checks the tree against both: no file may be added,
removed or changed without a record. The four things that vkxp adds (`MANIFEST.sha256`,
`PATCHES.md`, `README.vkxp.md` and the contents of `patches/`) are not part of the release.

The MIT licence of the vkxp repository does not cover this directory. Ruby is under the Ruby

and `GPL`. `README` is the release's own. Some files have terms of their own, which `LEGAL`
or the file itself gives. Of the vendored files these are:

| Oniguruma, the regular expression engine, which is part of this release: `regcomp.c`, `regenc.c`, `regenc.h`, `regerror.c`, `regexec.c`, `regint.h`, `regparse.c`, `regparse.h`, `regsyntax.c`, `include/ruby/oniguruma.h` and the encodings `enc/*.c` | BSD 2-clause (K. Kosako); it follows the licence of Ruby when distributed with it (`LEGAL`) |
| `parse.c` | generated by Bison: the GPL with the exception for generated parsers (`LEGAL`) |
| `util.c` (`ruby_strtod` and `ruby_dtoa` by David M. Gay, `ruby_qsort` from `mm.c`) | the permissive notices in `LEGAL` |
| `random.c` (MT19937) | BSD 3-clause, in the file |
| `st.c`, `include/ruby/st.h` | public domain (`LEGAL`) |
| `vsnprintf.c`, which `sprintf.c` includes | BSD (University of California), in the file |
| `strftime.c` | public domain, in the file |
| `enc/trans/*.c` | generated by the release from tables under the Ruby licence, which derive from Unicode and vendor mapping data |
| `ext/zlib/zlib.c` and the other extensions under `ext/` | the Ruby licence |

Unlike the vendored 1.8.7, no file under the LGPL is involved.

## How the subset was chosen

The release has 3432 files; 283 are kept, in four groups.

- **To build the interpreter.** The C files of the build list of
  `crates/vkxp-ruby192-sys/build.rs`: those the release's own build puts into
  `libruby-static.a`, with `miniprelude.c` for the prelude that the release generates and
  `dmydln.c` for `dln.c`; the encodings `enc/utf_16le.c`, `enc/shift_jis.c` and
  `enc/iso_8859_1.c` and the transcoders `enc/trans/japanese_sjis.c`,
  `enc/trans/single_byte.c` and `enc/trans/utf_16_32.c`, which are what the original
  runtime has beside the encodings of the core; and the `Zlib` binding `ext/zlib/zlib.c`.
  With them every file of the tree that the compiler opens while it compiles them, and
  nothing else: the headers of the top directory and of `include/`, the generated `.inc`
  files, and the C files that others include (`vm_exec.c`, `vm_eval.c`, `vm_insnhelper.c`,
  `vm_method.c`, `eval_error.c`, `eval_jump.c`, `thread_pthread.c`, `id.c`, `lex.c`,
  `vsnprintf.c`). The list was taken from the dependency output of the compiler (`-MM`).
  Every generated source is shipped by the release; nothing is generated when vkxp is
  built. `ruby/config.h`, the one file `configure` would write, lives in
  `crates/vkxp-ruby192-sys/config/`.
- **To run Ruby's own tests.** `main.c` and `ext/stringio/stringio.c`, `ext/fcntl/fcntl.c`,
  `ext/etc/etc.c`, `ext/continuation/continuation.c` and `ext/fiber/fiber.c` for the test
  executable; `bootstraptest/`, `test/runner.rb` and `test/ruby/` as the suites, without
  `test/ruby/enc/`, whose files test the encodings of the release one by one and are not
  run; and of `lib/` the files the runs load (`test/unit` and `minitest/unit` with
  `delegate`, `fileutils`, `open3`, `optparse`, `pathname`, `pp`, `prettyprint`, `rational`,
  `tempfile`, `thread`, `timeout` and `tmpdir`), found by recording the files the test
  processes opened. None of these is part of the interpreter that vkxp links.
- **For provenance.** `parse.y`, `defs/keywords` and `insns.def`, the sources of `parse.c`,
  `lex.c` and the instruction tables.
- **Licence.** `COPYING`, `COPYING.ja`, `GPL`, `LEGAL`, `README`.

Everything else is left out: the prelude sources, `enc/encdb.c` and `enc/trans/transdb.c`
(no name of an encoding or transcoder that is not linked is declared), every other encoding
and transcoder, `missing/` (the C library has every function), the rest of `ext/` and
`lib/`, documentation, `configure` and the other ports.
